extracted.intended_audience: Predoctoral fellowship applicants (NIH F31 - diversity) and their mentors/administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH F31 (PA-16-308) individual predoctoral fellowship (diversity) application, including required forms, biosketches, sponsor statements, vertebrate animal justification, facilities description, and training plan for peer review and agency processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF424 (R&R) required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required SF424 fields such as type of submission, dates, applicant information (legal name, DUNS, address), authorized representative, project title, project start/end dates, congressional district, and performance site location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark application type (New/Resubmission/Continuation), indicate whether application is submitted to other agencies, and provide organizational identifiers and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances (authorized representative signature)
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, authorized representative certifies statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances and agrees to comply with resulting terms if award is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorized representative must acknowledge awareness that false statements may subject them to criminal/civil/administrative penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). The certifications list is contained in the announcement or agency specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract and Project Narrative required
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a Project Summary/Abstract and a Project Narrative as specified in application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files in this sample: F31_Summary_Abstract.pdf and F31_Project_Narrative.pdf. Ensure these components address significance, aims, and public health relevance as required by FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents and required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Table of Contents enumerating all required sections and attachments (e.g., Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Applicant's Background and Goals; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Sponsor and Co-Sponsor Statements; Vertebrate Animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure page numbers and filenames for attachments are provided and that each required section is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH: DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES. Include name, eRA Commons user name, position title, education/training, and personal statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach biographical sketch and Current & Pending Support. Follow NIH biosketch sections and formatting limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For PD/PI and key personnel provide profile information including role category, position/title, organization, contact info, degree type/year, attached biosketch and current & pending support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), provide credential/eRA Commons user name when available, and include file names for attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims and Research Strategy presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Specific Aims and a Research Strategy attachment(s) with the experimental plan, rationale, and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are core review components; ensure aims are clear, testable, and matched to the research plan and training goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe available institutional and laboratory facilities, dedicated space, equipment, and core resources that will support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List lab square footage, tissue culture space, equipment (CO2 incubators, microscopes, centrifuges, PCR machines including real time, gel imaging, flow cytometer details, ultracentrifuges, freezers), core facilities, and fee-for-service resources. Indicate accreditation and staffing where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow cytometry/data acquisition QC
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of flow cytometry instrumentation and analysis pipelines (e.g., custom-made 4-laser BD Fortessa, FlowJo software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State quality control procedures such as running rainbow calibration beads within all experiments to allow cross comparison over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: affirmative declaration and IACUC status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used and whether IACUC review is pending or approved; provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify protocol numbers (e.g., IACUC UA protocol 08-102) and whether approval is pending/obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: justification for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide scientific justification for the use of animals and choice of species/strain/sex in addressing the research aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why animal models are necessary (e.g., lifelong infection models not feasible in humans), and justify sex selection (e.g., 'As to date, we have found no sex-associated difference ... we will use males dominantly for this study').

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: experimental procedures and endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe animal procedures (harvests, bleeding methods, infection routes, adoptive transfers), veterinary care, analgesia/anesthesia, monitoring, and euthanasia methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include methods to minimize discomfort (use of isoflurane, analgesia), criteria to halt procedures if distress occurs, and euthanasia method (e.g., isoflurane overdose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals: statistical justification of group sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide power calculations and rationale for sample sizes to ensure statistical power for detecting biologically meaningful differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: using 8 animals/group allows detection of >30% difference with 80% power at p<0.05; base calculations on preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal facility accreditation and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Document that animal housing and procedures occur in accredited facilities and that a full-time veterinarian and support staff oversee the animal program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State AAALAC accreditation and compliance with NIH and applicable federal/state/local regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects and clinical trial flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether human subjects are involved, whether the project is exempt, IRB review pending/approved, and provide Human Subject Assurance number if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required human subjects sections; indicate clinical trial status (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental, historic, and international activity declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether the project impacts the environment, whether an EA/EIS has been performed, whether research site is eligible as historic place, and whether activities involve international collaboration or activities outside the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanations and country identification if international activities exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget/Estimated Project Funding fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide budget summary including total federal funds requested, total non-federal funds, total federal & non-federal funds, and estimated program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure budget entries are complete and consistent with proposed scope and period (start/end dates provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Background and Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe applicant qualifications, prior training, specific goals for fellowship training, planned coursework and professional development activities, and expected outcomes for research career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include planned course attendance, meetings, presentation expectations (poster/oral at meetings), thesis committee schedule, frequency of mentor meetings, and timeline for manuscript/committee preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor and Co-Sponsor statements on mentoring and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must describe mentoring commitment, frequency of meetings, oversight mechanisms (lab meetings, committee reviews), and institutional/investigator resources relevant to training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail mentor's active research programs, collaborative projects, opportunities for trainee exposure (seminars, interest groups), and how sponsor will support trainee development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of institutional environment and commitment to training
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the broader institutional environment (departmental resources, cross-disciplinary programs, research centers, core facilities) and commitment to trainee development and diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of collaborative environment, seminar series, training courses, and statistics (e.g., graduate diversity percentage) where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and assay specification in Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify experimental methods and assays to be used (e.g., qPCR, plaque assay, flow cytometry, quantitative real-time PCR) and reference appropriate methods and prior publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite methodological references and standard protocols (e.g., plaque assay methods, PCR methods) so reviewers can assess feasibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a comprehensive Bibliography & References Cited section documenting prior work, supporting rationale, and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations and ensure in-text references align with the reference list; include key foundational and recent literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/Material use and copyright/FOIA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that application text is copyrighted by the awardee and sample applications are posted with permission for educational use; FOIA requests may lead to redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shared material only for nonprofit educational purposes provided the material remains unchanged and proper credit is given. Understand NIH will redact confidential commercial/financial info, reviewer comments, deliberations, and personal privacy information in FOIA responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure application materials are accessible and conform to Section 508; contact NIH office if accessibility problems occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample was reformatted for accessibility; if trouble accessing content, contact NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative attachments and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required administrative attachments such as Certification Letter, Cover Letter, Sponsor statements, and any other FOA-specified letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide filenames and ensure attachments are included in the Research & Related Other Project Information and Other Attachments sections.
